title: WebRL: Training LLM Web Agents via Self-Evolving Online Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
data_curation: Training and evaluation use the WebArena environment (5 sites: Reddit, GitLab, CMS, OpenStreetMap, OneStopShop). WebArena-Lite supplies 1,186 training samples (instruction + trajectory + reward function) and 165 test cases; its ~1k oracle trajectories are deemed too few alone. The self-evolving curriculum generates new tasks via in-breadth evolving (WizardLM-style) seeded from instructions the model failed in prior phases. Each phase keeps 500 generated instructions after a two-step filter: critic-score threshold between 0.05 and 0.75, then GPT-4o removes WebArena-infeasible tasks via per-site rules. Only successful trajectories enter the replay buffer. The ORM training set is built by rewriting WebArena-Lite instructions (varying place/product names) and collecting rollouts from all baselines, yielding 12,200 labeled samples using the reward function as ground truth.
curriculum: Two-stage pipeline. Part 1: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of the base model on the WebArena-Lite training set; the SFT model seeds both the replay buffer (with successful trajectories) and the failure set (instructions it could not solve). Part 2: an 8-phase self-evolving curriculum RL loop. Each phase generates ~500 new, critic-filtered instructions from the failure set, rolls out the actor, labels success via the ORM, then trains actor and critic on new rollouts mixed with replayed history. Task difficulty rises progressively because seeds come from prior failures and generated instructions grow more complex. Historical replay data is capped at 2x the new-interaction volume and selected by actor-confidence perplexity in [1/0.95, 1/0.5], so the agent revisits moderately-difficult successes while avoiding over-familiar or still-too-hard ones.
method: WebRL is an off-policy actor-critic RL algorithm for web agents with binary terminal reward, targeting task scarcity, sparse feedback, and policy drift. An outcome-supervised reward model (ORM), an LLM outputting YES/NO over (instruction, action history, final-state HTML), supplies the 0/1 reward for newly generated tasks lacking a reward function. The policy objective is maximum-entropy RL with a KL term tying the current policy πθ to the previous phase's policy πref: max E[r + β log πref] + βH(πθ). Derived as a Q*-to-policy mapping (Rafailov 2024), the loss is L = Eν[β log(πθ/πref) − A*]², which both raises good-action and lowers bad-action probability. Advantage A is estimated via a value network trained by cross-entropy classification (Farebrother 2024) with GAE (λ=0.5, γ=0.9). A replay buffer with actor-confidence (perplexity) filtering prevents forgetting. Contrasted with DPO (no pairwise data needed), PPO (off-policy vs on-policy), and AWR (explicitly reduces wrong-action probability).
eval_metrics: Evaluation is on WebArena-Lite (165 test cases across 5 sites) using task success rate (SR). WebRL lifts Llama-3.1-8B from 4.8% to 42.4%, GLM-4-9B from 6.1% to 43%, and Llama-3.1-70B from 12.7% to 49.1%, beating GPT-4-Turbo (17.6%), GPT-4o (13.9%), and prior open-LLM SOTA AutoWebGLM (18.2%); per-site highs include GitLab 46.7% and CMS 54.3% for Llama-8B. ORM accuracy reaches ~80% on the test set and 100 manually-labeled rollouts, above GPT-4/Captioner+GPT-4/GPT-4V baselines (~70-73%). Ablations confirm the replay buffer, KL-constrained update, and curriculum each contribute; the perplexity window [1/0.95,1/0.5] and moderate β are optimal. Additional analyses cover error-type distribution, performance by step count and complexity, and stability across 4 seeds and 3 generation prompts.
key_results: Llama-3.1-8B + WebRL: 4.8% to 42.4% SR on WebArena-Lite (vs GPT-4-Turbo 17.6%); Llama-3.1-70B reaches 49.1% and GLM-4-9B reaches 43%. The trained 8B ORM verifies success at ~80% accuracy, exceeding GPT-4-based verifiers (~70-73%).
evolution_note: WebRL builds on DigiRL/AWR actor-critic online RL and WizardLM-style evol-instruct task generation, reacting to DigiRL's fixed task set by adding a self-evolving curriculum and KL-anchored off-policy updates. In the 2024 wave of agentic RL it shows open LLMs can surpass proprietary APIs on web tasks, motivating later self-play and curriculum-driven agent RL for computer-use agents.
